nodes.title: Round 5 QA pass 1 (base 5148982, prod build + Neon TEST + real Azure, Playwright phone 393x876 touch + laptop 1440x900, 22:40-00:30 IST): 19 defects (2 P0, 10 P1, 7 P2), 5 fixed on claude/r5-qa. WebRTC transcription call opened 0 of 20 lessons in the container (UDP), so all ran in the recording fallback. POST /api/lesson/start n=21: min 3.1 s, p50 6.4 s (load-inflated), max 12.9 s. TTS lines are raw PCM, 398-497 KB per line; Slow 3G + 4x CPU n=1: first word 17.4 s after navigation. docs/design/round5/qa/DEFECTS.md

A tap-to-talk press before the cascade's WebRTC transcription call is up was lost: the tail committed to a closed data channel, or the 10 s fallback reset `talking` mid-press; no answer, no child_silent, floor stuck on Listening. Fixed in cascadeLink.ts: such a press records locally and uploads (9/9 spoken runs answered after the fix)

The Parent-corner unlock is server-side for 10 min and cleared only by a pagehide beacon; a killed tab (Android swipe-away) left it open, and a new tab walked into the corner without the PIN. Fixed in Gate.tsx: the first gate check of a page load never trusts a leftover unlock

A tab open across a deploy hit a 404 lazy chunk (err.resource Landing-*.js) and the route error page's Home link re-requested the same chunk, so the page was dead. Fixed: src/app/staleBuild.ts reloads once on vite:preloadError or a chunk-load route error (30 s loop guard); Home reloads the document

QA spoken answers: Chromium's --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture loops the WAV per capture source, from an instant the page cannot see; a second getUserMedia stream plays its own loop. Align presses on a clone of the APP's own mic track (same source, own enabled flag) and keep every uploaded clip to check for clipped starts. Reverse if Chromium exposes the fake source's position

Method: `npx vite build` served by server/serve.mjs with tests/prod/prod-routing.env against the Neon TEST branch and real Azure models; Playwright + /opt/pw-browsers/chromium; phone 393x876 dpr 2.75 touch Android UA, laptop 1440x900; spoken answers from Azure Speech hi-IN-AnanyaNeural WAVs via the fake mic. Numbers: 20 lessons started (kept logs), WebRTC transcription call opened 0/20 (container limit); POST /api/lesson/start server ms n=21 min 3075, p50 6403, max 12857 (upper half with 2-4 parallel lessons and/or the test suite running); GET /api/child/map 189,492 B, 2.7-6.6 s, fetched twice per lesson start before the fix, once after; TTS stream bodies 398,873 B (106 chars) and 497,333 B (113 chars); Slow 3G (400 ms RTT, 400 kbit/s) + 4x CPU n=1: navigation to her first word 17.4 s, last caption 23.5 s, Your turn 44.5 s. ## r5-qa-fake-mic-second-stream
Tried (2026-10-14): finding the fake mic's loop position for QA spoken answers by opening a second getUserMedia stream in the page and timing speech onsets on it. What broke: Chromium plays the fake WAV loop per capture stream, so the second stream's onsets were unrelated to the app's; presses landed mid-phrase and ASR heard fragments ('किलो में क्या अंतर है?', 'करो'), which first looked like an app defect (clipped recording). The uploaded clip (4.56 s for a 4.3 s press, speech from 0 s) proved the app recorded everything. Replaced by dc-r5-qa-fake-mic-alignment (clone the app's own track). Reverse if: never; check uploaded clips whenever ASR looks truncated.
